chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad: 'May I be your ransom, tell me about the saying of Allah: 'And those Foremost (in Faith) will be Foremost (in the Hereafter). These are they who are drawn nigh (to Allah)'?' He said: 'Allah spoke of this on the day He determined the creation in the Covenant, two thousand years before creating the creatures.' I said: 'Explain this to me.' He said: 'When Allah willed to create the creation, He created them from clay, and raised a fire for them and said: Enter it. The first to enter it were Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, and the Commander of the Faithful, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and nine of the Imams, an Imam after an Imam. Then their followers followed them. They are, by Allah, the Foremost.'

key_terms.إِمَامٌ بَعْدَ إِمَامٍ: An Imam after an Imam (succession of Imams)

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Foremost' (Al-Sabiqun) mentioned in the Quran according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba* anchors the concept of *Sabiqun* (the Foremost) in the Shia doctrine of *al-Mithaq* (the Primordial Covenant), asserting that the Prophet, Ahl al-Bayt, and the Twelve Imams were pre-eminently chosen before creation. It specifically identifies the 'Foremost' as the Prophet, Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and the nine subsequent Imams, who entered the Fire (or were tested) first, thereby establishing their unique ontological status as *al-Muqarrabun* (the Drawn Nigh). This interpretation reinforces the Shia belief in the pre-existence and superior spiritual rank of the Imams, linking their earthly mission to a cosmic event prior to the creation of Adam.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (20) Ali bin al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya from Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali from Muhammad bin Sinan that Dawood bin Katheer ar-Riqqi had said:

I said to Abu Abdullah Ja’far bin Muhammad as-Sadiq (as): “May I die for you! Would you tell me about (the meaning of) the saying of Allah, “And those Foremost (in Faith) will be Foremost (in the Hereafter). These are they who are drawn nigh (to Allah)”? He said: “Allah has said that on the day when He has determined the creation in the Covenant two thousand years before creating the creatures (people).” I said: “Would you explain this for me?” He said: “When Allah had willed to create people, He made them of clay and made a fire for them. He ordered them to enter into fire. The first ones, who had entered into it, were Muhammad, Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and nine imams one after the other and then their followers followed them. By Allah they are the foremost.”
